SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told with the same weight as David rejected by his elder brothers before he faces Goliath (Christian pillar), Odysseus disguised as a beggar in his own hall (Greek pillar), or the young Sigurd unknown as Sigmund's son (Norse pillar) -- a hidden hero proving himself. DISTRACTOR MINE: other Arthurian disguised-hero arrivals (Perceval the country boy at Camelot; Galahad the pure knight -- both DIFFERENT), other kitchen-boys (there aren't others), other coloured-knights (Sir Gawain's Green Knight is a WHOLLY DIFFERENT figure from the Green Knight Gareth defeats), other 'Beaumains' (there aren't others). Wrong father: KING LOT OF ORKNEY (making Gareth Gawain's brother and Arthur's nephew), not King Ban.
history_overlap: None with history.

name: The Grail as the cup of the Last Supper: Joseph of Arimathea to Britain
scope: The identification of the Grail with the Last Supper cup carried to Britain by Joseph of Arimathea, from Robert de Boron's Joseph d'Arimathie (c.1200), the Vulgate Estoire del Saint Graal (c.1220), and Malory Book XI. T1: in Chretien de Troyes's original Perceval (c.1181-90), the 'graal' is only a WIDE SERVING-DISH borne by a maiden in a procession -- it is not identified with any Christian relic and no origin is given. ROBERT DE BORON, writing in French verse c.1200, is the one who IDENTIFIES the Grail with the CUP OF THE LAST SUPPER at which Jesus said 'this is my blood'. T2: in Robert de Boron's Joseph d'Arimathie, JOSEPH OF ARIMATHEA (the man who in the Gospels asks Pilate for Jesus's body and buries him in his own tomb) is credited with two acts: first, he receives the CUP from the Last Supper (whether given by Jesus or preserved by him); second, at the crucifixion he uses the same cup to CATCH SOME OF THE BLOOD flowing from Jesus's side when the Roman soldier Longinus pierces him with the LANCE. The cup thus contains BOTH the memory of the wine of the Last Supper AND actual drops of Christ's blood. T3: after the crucifixion, Joseph is imprisoned (Robert de Boron says by the Jews of Jerusalem) but the risen Jesus visits him in prison and gives him the SECRETS of the Grail -- a small liturgy Joseph is to keep and teach to a chosen family. Joseph is fed by the Grail during forty-two years in prison. Freed by the Emperor Vespasian, Joseph gathers his family and companions and travels WEST, eventually reaching BRITAIN, where he founds the first church at GLASTONBURY. T4: at Glastonbury Joseph plants his THORN-STAFF in the ground and it takes root as a HAWTHORN TREE that flowers on Christmas Day every year -- the Glastonbury Thorn is a real winter-flowering hawthorn cultivar that DID grow on Wearyall Hill at Glastonbury until it was vandalised in 2010 (and cuttings survive). This legend gave Glastonbury Abbey its later prestige as the 'oldest Christian foundation in England'. T5: the Grail passes down Joseph's descendants -- the FISHER KINGS -- for generations at CORBENIC, the Grail Castle. Each Fisher King guards it; each grows old; and each is wounded by a mysterious stroke (the DOLOROUS STROKE) that will only be healed when the destined Grail Knight comes and asks the right question. This is the Grail sought in the Vulgate Queste and in Malory Book XVII -- achieved by Galahad. Further rungs: Robert de Boron's Joseph d'Arimathie (c.1200) is the SINGLE most influential source for the 'Grail as Last Supper cup' identification; the Vulgate Estoire del Saint Graal (c.1220) expands the story into a full history of the Grail; the GLASTONBURY THORN is a real cultivar (Crataegus monogyna 'Biflora') that does flower twice a year -- the myth attaches to a real botanical oddity; the same Glastonbury Abbey that promoted the Joseph legend also 'discovered' Arthur's grave in 1191 (both probably medieval promotion to draw pilgrims); Wolfram von Eschenbach's Parzival gives a WHOLLY DIFFERENT Grail-origin (the Grail as a stone fallen from heaven -- see next ladder).
source: PRIMARY: Robert de Boron, Joseph d'Arimathie (Old French verse and later prose Estoire, c.1200 -- Joseph receives the Last Supper cup, catches Christ's blood at the crucifixion, is imprisoned, freed, travels west, brings the Grail to Britain). Vulgate Cycle, Estoire del Saint Graal (c.1220 -- expanded history). Sir Thomas Malory, Le Morte d'Arthur, Book XI (Grail Castle at Corbenic, King Pelles as Fisher King), Book XVII (achievement of the Grail). CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'Holy Grail' and 'Joseph of Arimathea' and 'Glastonbury Thorn' (403; via browser 2026-09-04) and Wikipedia 'Holy Grail', 'Joseph of Arimathea', 'Robert de Boron', 'Glastonbury Thorn', 'Glastonbury Abbey', 'Fisher King' -- Chretien's original graal-as-dish, Robert de Boron's identification with the Last Supper cup, catching the blood at the crucifixion, forty-two years in prison, Vespasian's release, travel to Britain, Glastonbury and the Thorn, Corbenic and the Fisher Kings, Malory's Grail. CORROBORATE AT BUILD: exact date of Robert de Boron's Joseph d'Arimathie (usually given as c.1191-1202).
framing_note: The GRAIL-ORIGIN ladder. Dinner-test payoffs: T2 (the Grail is BOTH the Last Supper cup AND the cup that CAUGHT CHRIST'S BLOOD at the crucifixion) and T4 (the GLASTONBURY THORN -- Joseph's staff planted in England takes root and flowers on Christmas every year -- and there's a REAL cultivar that does this). ANTI-RESTATEMENT: never let the stem say 'the cup of the Last Supper brought to Britain' AND ask its bearer's name; describe the SCENE (the cup at the supper, the cup at the cross catching blood, forty-two years in prison, a journey west, a staff planted at Glastonbury flowering on Christmas) and let the recall be the OBJECT (the Grail / the Cup), the BEARER (Joseph of Arimathea), the PLACE (Glastonbury), or the DETAIL (the flowering thorn on Christmas Day). SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told with the same weight as the Ark of the Covenant carried to Israel (Christian/Jewish pillar; NOT out-of-lane -- it's Old Testament heritage), the Nine Worthies tradition, the relics of the True Cross -- a sacred object with a journey and a home. Do NOT frame in 'the Lord' or 'fulfilled the prophecy' language; use plain narrative: 'Joseph of Arimathea', 'the cup', 'Britain'. Note honestly at build-time that this is 12th-century French legend, not New Testament material -- the Gospels do NOT connect Joseph of Arimathea with the cup or with Britain. DISTRACTOR MINE: other legendary carriers of Christian relics (Helena mother of Constantine finding the True Cross -- Christian pillar; the Turin Shroud -- Christian pillar), other Grail origins (WOLFRAM'S Grail as a STONE FROM HEAVEN -- next ladder, MUST distinguish), other Joseph figures (there is Joseph the patriarch, Joseph husband of Mary, Joseph of Arimathea -- three DIFFERENT Josephs). Wrong Grail-origin: Robert de Boron identifies it with the LAST SUPPER CUP; Wolfram von Eschenbach makes it a STONE. Wrong bearer to Britain: JOSEPH OF ARIMATHEA (not Joseph husband of Mary, not the patriarch Joseph). HISTORICAL vs LEGENDARY: the Joseph-of-Arimathea-to-Britain legend is 12th-century French invention; it has no historical basis. State honestly if asked.
history_overlap: HISTORY owns Glastonbury Abbey as a real medieval institution and its two famous forgeries (Arthur's grave 1191 and the Joseph-of-Arimathea claim). GEOGRAPHY owns Glastonbury as a Somerset place. Theology owns the STORY of Joseph, the cup, and the flowering staff.

name: The Grail procession: bleeding lance, sword, platter, and cup
scope: The mystical procession that passes through the Fisher King's hall, from Chretien de Troyes's Perceval le Conte du Graal (c.1181-90) and Malory Book XVII. T1: at CORBENIC (the Grail Castle), during supper at the FISHER KING'S table, a MYSTICAL PROCESSION passes through the hall from door to door on certain nights. The knight who happens to be there for the night sees it and must decide whether to ask about it. T2: in Chretien's original the procession consists of FOUR (or three, versions differ) elements borne by different figures: (1) a YOUNG MAN carries a WHITE LANCE from whose tip a drop of BLOOD constantly falls and runs down his hand; (2) TWO YOUNG MEN each carry a golden CANDELABRUM with ten burning candles; (3) a MAIDEN in fine clothes carries the GRAAL (a shallow serving-dish or platter of gold, set with precious stones and giving off a great light); (4) a SECOND MAIDEN carries a SILVER PLATTER (Chretien: 'un tailleoir d'argent'). T3: in the Vulgate Queste and in Malory, the procession is CHRISTIANISED. The bleeding LANCE becomes the LANCE OF LONGINUS -- the Roman soldier's lance that pierced Christ's side at the crucifixion -- and it bleeds because it once tasted holy blood. The GRAAL becomes the CUP OF THE LAST SUPPER that also caught Christ's blood. The SWORD (Malory adds a sword in some versions) is the SWORD OF DAVID or a broken sword of the maimed king. The PLATTER is variously the platter of the Last Supper. Every object is a relic. T4: the WOUNDED KING at whose supper the procession passes is the FISHER KING (in Malory, KING PELLES). His wound was given by the DOLOROUS STROKE of Sir BALIN, who in an earlier tale drove a spear (in fact the Lance of Longinus itself, taken from a chapel wall) through the king's thighs. The wound will not heal because the same lance would have to be brought to touch it, and the WHOLE LAND ROUND CORBENIC IS THE WASTE LAND while its king lies wounded. T5: the questing knight must ASK THE QUESTION as the procession passes: 'WHOM DOES THE GRAIL SERVE?' (Chretien) or 'What ails you, king?' (later versions). Perceval fails, keeps silent, and the wound stays open and the land stays waste. GALAHAD, when he comes in Malory Book XVII, ASKS RIGHTLY, sees the Grail uncovered, and receives communion from Christ himself. Later at Corbenic Galahad also touches the Fisher King's wound with drops of blood from the Lance, and the king is healed and the Waste Land restored (Malory Book XVII ch.21). Further rungs: Chretien's four-element procession (lance, candles, graal, platter) is the ORIGINAL; the Christianising into Longinus's lance + Last Supper cup is by Robert de Boron and the Vulgate; the DOLOROUS STROKE tale (Sir Balin unwittingly wounding a king with a holy lance) is developed in the Vulgate Cycle and the Post-Vulgate Suite du Merlin; the WASTE LAND motif (a king wounded, a kingdom sterile until the question is answered) is the deepest myth-pattern in the Grail cycle and directly inspires T.S. Eliot's 1922 poem 'The Waste Land'.
source: PRIMARY: Chretien de Troyes, Perceval, le Conte du Graal (c.1181-90 -- the four-element procession: bleeding lance, candelabra, graal-dish, silver platter). Robert de Boron, Joseph d'Arimathie (c.1200 -- Christianising of the objects). Vulgate Cycle, Queste del Saint Graal (c.1220 -- Galahad's success; Lance of Longinus identified). Sir Thomas Malory, Le Morte d'Arthur, Book XI (Corbenic and Pelles), Book XVII chapter 21 (Galahad heals the Fisher King with the Lance). Vulgate/Post-Vulgate Suite du Merlin (c.1230-40 -- Balin's Dolorous Stroke). CORROBORATE AT BUILD: exact number of candles in Chretien's candelabra (Chretien says ten each).
framing_note: The PROCESSION ladder -- the mystical heart of the Grail scene. Dinner-test payoffs: T2 (the details of the procession -- a WHITE LANCE with a DROP OF BLOOD constantly falling from its tip, borne by a young man) and T4 (the Fisher King's wound was given by the very LANCE he now sees pass, driven through his thighs long ago by Sir Balin's mistake). ANTI-RESTATEMENT: never let the stem say 'the mystical objects that pass through the Grail Castle' AND ask what they are; describe the SCENE (supper at Corbenic, a lance whose tip drips blood, a maiden bearing a bright dish, a wounded king watching from his couch) and let the recall be the LANCE, the LANCE-BEARER (Longinus in Christianised versions), the DISH (graal / cup), or the QUESTION. SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told with the same weight as the tabernacle procession in Israel (Christian/Jewish pillar), Odin's procession of the einherjar to Valhalla (Norse pillar), or the Eleusinian Mysteries procession (Greek pillar) -- a sacred procession of relics whose meaning demands the right response. DISTRACTOR MINE: other mystical processions (there aren't many at this scale), other bleeding-lances (only ONE -- the Lance of Longinus), other Grail knights (Perceval FAILS to ask, Galahad SUCCEEDS -- must distinguish), other wounded kings (only the FISHER KING at Corbenic). Wrong wound-giver: SIR BALIN with the LANCE OF LONGINUS taken from a chapel wall (called the DOLOROUS STROKE). Wrong number of Grail knights: THREE achieve the Grail in Malory -- Galahad, Percival, Bors -- but ONLY Galahad heals the Fisher King.
history_overlap: None with history. Symmetric-voice note: the Christianising of the procession into Longinus's lance and the Last Supper cup is 12th-13th c. French legend, not Gospel material. State honestly.

name: Wolfram's Parzival: the Grail as a stone from heaven
scope: Wolfram von Eschenbach's alternative Grail-tradition, in his Middle High German epic Parzival (c.1200-1210). T1: WOLFRAM VON ESCHENBACH was a Bavarian knight-poet (born c.1160-70, wrote c.1200-1210) who composed PARZIVAL -- a huge Middle High German epic of about 25,000 lines in rhymed couplets -- as a continuation and RETELLING of Chretien de Troyes's unfinished Perceval. Wolfram's poem is the greatest German Arthurian romance. T2: Wolfram's PARZIVAL is a MUCH more elaborate story than Chretien's: it begins with Parzival's father GAHMURET journeying to the East, marrying the black African queen BELACANE, having a piebald son FEIREFIZ (half black, half white -- Parzival's half-brother), then returning west and marrying Herzeloyde who bears Parzival. It follows Parzival from birth to Grail-kingship in about 800 pages. T3: Wolfram's GRAIL IS NOT A CUP. Wolfram calls it 'LAPSIT EXILLIS' (a garbled Latin phrase in Wolfram's own text -- 'lapis exilis'? 'lapis ex caelis'? Wolfram's meaning has been debated for centuries) -- a STONE. Specifically, a stone that FELL FROM HEAVEN, brought down from the sky by angels who stayed NEUTRAL in the war between God and Lucifer. It is kept at the Grail Castle MUNSALVAESCHE (the Mountain of Salvation) and served by an order of GRAIL KNIGHTS called the TEMPLEISEN (echoing the historical Knights Templar). T4: Wolfram's Grail-stone has powers different from the cup: it FEEDS whoever looks upon it with whatever food they most desire; a single glance at it prolongs life so that a man who sees it will not die within a week; the NAMES of new Grail Knights appear as writing on its surface (which fades once read); and once a year on GOOD FRIDAY a WHITE DOVE descends from heaven and lays a WAFER on the stone, which replenishes its power. T5: at the end of Wolfram's poem, Parzival at last returns to Munsalvaesche, asks the Fisher King (his uncle ANFORTAS) 'WHAT AILS YOU, UNCLE?', and by asking heals the wound; Parzival becomes the new Grail King, his wife CONDWIRAMURS and their sons join him; his black-and-white half-brother FEIREFIZ (who cannot see the Grail because he is a pagan) is baptised and can then see it; Feirefiz marries the Grail-bearer REPANSE DE SCHOYE, and their son becomes PRESTER JOHN, the legendary Christian king of the far East. Further rungs: Wolfram's Parzival is the direct source of Richard Wagner's opera PARSIFAL (1882); Wolfram claims his source is a Provencal poet named 'Kyot' who supposedly worked from an Arabic-Jewish text found in Toledo -- most modern scholars think Kyot is Wolfram's invention (Wolfram teases his rivals by claiming a superior source they cannot check); 'lapsit exillis' has been proposed as 'lapis exilis' (small stone), 'lapis ex caelis' (stone from heaven), 'lapis elixir' (philosopher's stone from alchemy), 'lapis lapsus ex caelis' (stone fallen from heaven) -- all guesses; the FEIREFIZ / PRESTER JOHN thread ties the Grail into the medieval European legend of a great Christian king ruling in the far East beyond the Muslim world.

CORROBORATE AT BUILD: whether Wolfram's uncle-figure is named Anfortas or Amfortas (spellings vary between manuscripts and translations).
framing_note: The ALTERNATIVE-GRAIL ladder -- Wolfram is the SECOND great Grail tradition alongside the French cup-of-the-Last-Supper. Dinner-test payoffs: T3 (the Grail is NOT A CUP but a STONE FALLEN FROM HEAVEN, brought down by angels who stayed neutral in Lucifer's war) and T4 (once a year a WHITE DOVE lays a WAFER on the stone to renew it, and the NAMES of new Grail Knights appear as writing on its surface). ANTI-RESTATEMENT: never let the stem say 'the Grail as a stone from heaven' AND ask which author; describe the SCENE (an epic poem written c.1210 by a Bavarian knight, a Grail Castle called Munsalvaesche, a stone that feeds who looks on it, a dove on Good Friday) and let the recall be the AUTHOR (Wolfram von Eschenbach), the POEM (Parzival), the OBJECT (a stone, not a cup), or the DESCENT (Prester John). SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told with the same weight as the Norse World-Tree Yggdrasil (Norse pillar) or Odin's mead brewed from Kvasir's blood (Norse pillar) -- a sacred object with multiple layered properties. Note honestly that Wolfram's Grail-as-stone is a DIFFERENT tradition from the French Grail-as-cup; both are 12th-13th century literary inventions, not history. DISTRACTOR MINE: other Grail versions (Chretien's serving-dish, Robert de Boron's Last Supper cup, Malory's cup -- MUST distinguish Wolfram's stone), other stones-from-heaven (the Kaaba's Black Stone -- out-of-lane; the philosopher's stone -- alchemy, not Grail), other Grail Castles (Corbenic in Chretien/Malory vs Munsalvaesche in Wolfram -- both). Wrong Grail-form: Wolfram = STONE, not cup. Wrong author-nationality: WOLFRAM is BAVARIAN (German), not French like Chretien.
history_overlap: None with history. HISTORY may own the historical Knights Templar (1119-1312) which Wolfram's Templeisen echo. HISTORY may also own the medieval legend of Prester John as it appeared in real 12th-c. European diplomatic and geographical thought.

name: The Round Table Fellowship: knights, quests, and code
scope: The FELLOWSHIP of the Round Table as an institution and moral code, from Malory Le Morte d'Arthur throughout (Books III-XXI) and the earlier French Vulgate Cycle. T1: the ROUND TABLE FELLOWSHIP is Arthur's council of picked knights, seated at the round table at Camelot. Malory says the Round Table seats about 150 knights (Book III ch.1) -- though the number that gets remembered by name is a much smaller inner circle of a dozen or so: LANCELOT, GAWAIN, TRISTAN, GALAHAD, PERCIVAL, BORS, KAY, BEDIVERE, GARETH, GAHERIS, AGRAVAINE, MORDRED, LAMORAK, PALAMEDES, and about a dozen more. Each knight has a NAMED SEAT with the letters written in gold. T2: the fellowship is bound by an OATH, sworn each Pentecost at Camelot when the knights renew their vows. Malory (Book III ch.15) gives the oath in full: 'to do no outrage, nor murder, and always to flee treason; also, by no means to be cruel, but to give mercy unto him that asketh mercy; and always to do ladies, damsels, and gentlewomen and widows succour; and never to force ladies, damsels, and gentlewomen; and to no man for lucre to take battle in a wrongful quarrel for no law, nor for no world's goods'. This is the codification of CHIVALRY as Malory understood it. T3: the fellowship carries out QUESTS. Some are solitary (a knight leaves Camelot in search of adventure and returns to tell of it; Sir Marhaus, Sir Uwaine and Sir Gawain's three-year quest in Book IV is an example); some are collective (the QUEST OF THE HOLY GRAIL, Book XIII-XVII, in which most of the fellowship rides out and only three -- Galahad, Percival, Bors -- return alive). Every Pentecost the knights meet again and tell what they have done in the year; scribes write down each knight's adventures, which is Malory's fictional source for the book. T4: NOT ALL knights of the fellowship are equally good. Malory presents a hierarchy: LANCELOT is greatest in arms but flawed by his love for Guinevere; GALAHAD is the purest but only briefly present; GAWAIN is chivalrous but hot-tempered and vengeful; TRISTAN is a great knight but also an adulterer; KAY is competent but sharp-tongued; MORDRED is a member of the fellowship but the traitor who will destroy it. The fellowship's flaw is that a code of honour cannot save it from human weaknesses -- love, envy, pride. T5: the fellowship BREAKS in Books XX-XXI. Agravaine and Mordred expose Lancelot and Guinevere; Lancelot rescues her from the pyre and accidentally kills Gareth and Gaheris; Gawain demands revenge; Arthur pursues Lancelot to France; Mordred seizes the throne; Camlann kills every knight of the fellowship on both sides. When Arthur is carried to Avalon and Bedivere weeps on the shore, the fellowship is DEAD. Malory ends his book by naming which few knights survive to become hermits or die of grief -- and by the LATIN EPITAPH 'rex quondam rexque futurus'. Further rungs: the number 150 is Malory's, though counts vary (some say 140, some 'more than a hundred'); the Pentecost Oath is one of the earliest fully-articulated codes of chivalry in English literature; the FALL of the fellowship through internal moral failure (not external enemy) is the whole book's tragic shape; T.H. White's 'The Once and Future King' (1958) and Tennyson's Idylls of the King (1859) both make the fall of the fellowship their central theme.

CORROBORATE AT BUILD: exact Malory numbering of knights of the Round Table (multiple 'lists' exist in different manuscripts).
framing_note: The FELLOWSHIP-AS-INSTITUTION ladder -- the Round Table is not just furniture, it is an ORDER. Dinner-test payoffs: T2 (the OATH sworn at Pentecost -- 'to do no outrage, nor murder... to give mercy unto him that asketh mercy... to do ladies succour... never to force ladies') and T5 (the fellowship destroys itself through LOVE and VENGEANCE, not through any external enemy). ANTI-RESTATEMENT: never let the stem say 'the code of the Round Table' AND ask what it is called; describe the SCENE (a hundred and fifty knights seated round, an oath sworn at Pentecost each year, a scribe writing down what each did in the year past) and let the recall be the OATH-DAY (Pentecost), the NUMBER of seats (150), the DOOM (broken by love and revenge from within), or the SURVIVING KNIGHTS (three from the Grail Quest; two after Camlann). SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told with the same weight as Odin's einherjar in Valhalla (Norse pillar), the Fianna of Fionn in Ireland (Celtic pillar), the Twelve Apostles (Christian pillar) -- a sworn brotherhood whose story is both glory and fall. DISTRACTOR MINE: other Arthurian objects and institutions (Excalibur, the Grail, Camelot -- adjacent), other sworn brotherhoods (Fianna, apostles, einherjar), other codes (the Knights Templar Rule, the Bushido -- out-of-lane), other seat-counts (150 in Malory, 12 disciples in Christian pillar, 12 Peers of France in Roland -- Western-medieval pillar). Wrong oath-day: Pentecost, not Christmas or Easter. Wrong fatal cause: LOVE + VENGEANCE (Lancelot's love, Gawain's vengeance for his brothers), not any single external enemy.
history_overlap: HISTORY owns the actual medieval codes of chivalry and orders like the Templars, Hospitallers, Order of the Garter (founded by Edward III in 1348 in explicit imitation of Arthur's Round Table). Theology owns the STORY of the fellowship, the oath, the fall.
